Application Procedure
Graduate Admissions Process
To be considered for graduate admission at San Diego State University, you must follow the 4 step process outlined below. For more detailed information regarding the admissions process, please visit the Graduate Admissions Website (http://arweb.sdsu.edu/es/admissions/grad/index.html).
Step 1: Complete the CSU Cal State Apply Application by December 1
Each applicant must submit the California State University application electronically at the CSU Cal State Apply (https://www2.calstate.edu/apply) along with the $70 nonrefundable application fee. Once you have submitted a CSU Cal State Apply application, you will be assigned a RedID number (also called EMPLID or SDSUid), which will be e-mailed to you within 3-5 business days. Your RedID number will allow you to track the status of your application through the my.SDSU portal.
Please note that SDSU does not offer fee waivers for the CALSTATE Apply application fee.
Step 2: Submit Official Transcripts & Test Scores to the Graduate Admissions Office by December 15
After you have submitted the CSU Cal State Apply application and received your RedID number, you will need to send official transcripts and test scores to the Graduate Admissions Office. Sending transcripts before submitting the CSU Cal State Apply application will result in processing delays.
You must provide the following:
Official transcripts (in sealed envelopes) issued within the last year, from all U.S. colleges and universities attended. Students who previously attended SDSU need only submit transcripts for coursework completed since last attendance. Hard copy SDSU transcripts are not required.
Students with international coursework must submit both the official transcript and proof of degree. If documents are in a language other than English, they must be accompanied by a certified literal English translation. For country specific requirements, please see the Graduate Admissions website (link to http://arweb.sdsu.edu/es/admissions/grad/country.html).
General GRE test scores have been suspended and are NOT required.
Send TOEFL/IELTS/DET scores (if applicable) directly to SDSU (Institution Code: 4682).
TOEFL minimum score 4 or higher (exam taken on or after January 21, 2026) 80 or higher (exam taken before January 21, 2026)
IELTS overall score of 7.0 or higher: Score report must be submitted directly to the SDSU Graduate Admissions Office. Test score must be from within the past two years.
DET (Duolingo) overall score of 120 or higher: Score report must be submitted directly to the SDSU Graduate Admissions Office. Test score must be from within the past two years.
Test scores must be dated within two years of the start of the application filing period. Official test scores can be sent directly from the testing agency or can be uploaded through my.SDSU.
Various English proficiency waivers are available for applicants. Please review the Steps to Apply on the Graduate Admissions website for more information.
The above listed materials should be sent to:
Graduate Admissions Office
San Diego State University
5500 Campanile Drive
San Diego, CA 92182-8225
NOTE: Electronic transcripts may also be submitted. Go to https://registrar.sdsu.edu/students/transcripts/electronic_transcripts for additional information.
Important Reminder:
It is the student’s responsibility to ensure that all transcripts are submitted by the stated deadline. Please check your  MY.SDSU  account regularly for updates. The department  cannot  verify the status of your transcripts. For any questions regarding transcript receipt or processing, please contact  Graduate Admissions  or  International Admissions  directly.
Contact Information
General Admissions: admissions@sdsu.edu | (619) 594-6336
International Admissions: intladmission@sdsu.edu | (619) 594-6336
Program-specific questions: biojtdoc@sdsu.edu
STEP 3: Supplemental Graduate Application and Documents required by the BIOLOGY Department via SLATE.
Deadline: December 15
In addition to the CSU Cal State Apply application, applicants must also submit supplemental materials required by the Biology Department as follows:
Supplemental Graduate Application : Applicants will be automatically prompted to complete the SLATE program application after their Cal State Apply submission is received.
Statement of Professional Goals (usually one to three pages in length).
Resume or Curriculum Vitae
Three Letters of Recommendation. You will be asked to provide names and email addresses for individuals who will be writing your letters and uploading them onto the SLATE system themselves. The system allows for up to 5 letters.
Photocopy of TOEFL/IELTS and DET scores (foreign students only).
Copy of unofficial transcripts.
Review of applications for Fall 2027 will commence in early January 2027. In order to ensure consideration, please submit the CSU application, UC San Diego Application, Graduate Supplemental Application, and upload all necessary documents.
Tracking Your Application Status:
Use your Red I.D. number to track the status of your application online. You will be able to monitor when materials have been received and view a list of materials that are still required to complete your application file. Please bear in mind that we receive thousands of applications so it may take some time for the information to be added to your my.SDSU account.
STEP 4: Complete the UC San Diego Application
Deadline: December 15, 2026
Link: https://connect.grad.ucsd.edu/apply
Instructions:  JDP with SDSU
On the Program Selector page:
Degree Type: Doctor of Philosophy
Program Interest: Biological Sciences – Joint Doctoral Program with San Diego State University
Entry Term: Fall 2027
The UC San Diego application fee will be automatically waived for JDP applicants upon submission.
Required Materials for UC San Diego:
Statement of Purpose (SOP)
Transcripts
UC San Diego accepts unofficial transcripts (official transcripts required only if admitted).
SDSU requires official transcripts
CV/Resume
Three Letters of Recommendation
TOEFL/IELTS/DET Scores (International applicants only)
UC San Diego accepts self-reported scores (official scores required only if admitted).
SDSU requires official scores at the time of application.
Applicants must apply to both SDSU and UC San Diego and submit all required materials to each institution.
SDSU: Application fee required
UC San Diego: Application fee and international credential evaluation waived
For UC San Diego application system-related questions, contact: gradadmissions@ucsd.edu
Additional Important Notes to Follow
Please be sure to enter your SDSU Red ID number on the UC San Diego application.
Be sure to use the same name and email address on both the SDSU and UC San Diego applications to ensure proper matching of your materials.
If you are a current or former UC San Diego graduate student, please email the BioSci office at: biophdadmissions@ucsd.edu and request that your application be submitted.
Please note that applicants may NOT apply to both the UC San Diego stand alone Biology PhD program and the SDSU–UC San Diego Joint Doctoral Program (JDP). For additional details, please refer to: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/admission-faq/faq-general-application.html#can-i-apply-to-more-than-one-program-in-the-same-d.
